item.title: Artemis 1.0.0
item.description:
Artemis 1.0 is here, and it's open source under the GPL 3.0. Every part of the browser was gone through for this release, and more than 300 problems were fixed.

It needs macOS 26 or later on an M1 or newer Mac.

New

  • Built for liquid glass. Choose Glass in a space's theme, then set how frosted the sidebar and the window behind it are, all the way to clear.
  • Live folders fill themselves from a GitHub repo or a feed.
  • Hover over a pinned tab or a favourite to preview it. Mail tabs show what's new in your inbox.
  • ⌘Z undoes changes in the sidebar and in Settings.
  • Each space remembers which favourite it was showing.
  • Ask the page summarises the page, and offers what it knows when the page doesn't say.
  • A tab keeps a name you give it.
  • A count in a tab's title, like (12), shows as a badge.
  • Hold a dragged tab near the top or bottom of the sidebar and the list scrolls. The closer to the edge, the faster.

Refined

Privacy and security

  • Extensions only get what their permissions allow. Reading a site with your cookies, changing the proxy or reading the clipboard each need the permission the extension asked for.
  • Incognito leaves less behind. Certificates you accept, where downloads came from, and sites played in the mini-player are no longer saved.
  • A locked space asks for Touch ID as soon as you arrive on it, and keeps its pages out of menus and off the disk. Turning off its lock, deleting it or undoing a move out of it needs Touch ID.
  • A page asks before it starts a download.
  • Copied passwords and codes are hidden from clipboard managers and don't stay on the clipboard.
  • Clearing history also clears recently closed tabs, back and forward lists, and site icons from that time.
  • Search suggestions and site icons go through your profile's VPN extension, as pages do.

Windows and tabs

  • With several windows open, closing one no longer breaks sign-in popups, camera and microphone requests, or history in the tabs it opened.
  • With every window closed, ⌘T, History and the other commands open a new window.
  • ⇧⌘T brings back a group of closed tabs together, in order.
  • The sidebar's scroll bar is thinner and sits in the margin, clear of your tabs.
  • Delete Space asks first. So does removing an extension.

Mini-player

  • Pinch to resize it, even while another app is in front.
  • It sits flush against the side of the screen and moves between displays smoothly.

Your data

  • Passwords stay intact if Artemis is interrupted while saving them.
  • A session file that can't be read is set aside, never written over.
  • Restoring a backup keeps the profiles already on this Mac.

Quicker

  • History search keeps up with your typing, even with a large history.
  • Content blocking is ready sooner after a relaunch.
  • Installing an extension, exporting passwords and importing from another browser no longer pause the browser.

Fixed

  • Clicks on the floating sidebar no longer reach the page under it.
  • ⌘W in an incognito window closes the tab, not the window.
  • A page you trusted past a certificate warning never shows as Secure.
  • Local pages load their own stylesheets, images and linked pages.
  • The Now Playing bar and a tab's speaker show only while something plays.
  • Many smaller fixes across the sidebar, split view, the mini-player, the command bar, password autofill and VoiceOver.

item.title: Artemis 0.9.7
item.description:
It needs macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon.

New in 0.9.7

  • Addresses and cards. Artemis fills your saved addresses and cards from a list under the field, and offers to save new ones when you submit a form. Each profile keeps its own. Card numbers stay in your keychain and security codes are never saved.
  • You choose when to unlock. Passwords, cards and addresses each have their own setting: every time, after a few minutes, until you quit, or never. Locking your Mac or letting it sleep locks them all again.
  • Import from your other browsers. Bookmarks and history, into the profile you pick. It's in Settings › General.
  • Shortcuts and Siri. Open pages, switch spaces, find tabs, or grab the current page as Markdown. Showing your spaces and tabs in Spotlight is off until you turn it on in Settings › Privacy.
  • Unread badges. Sites can show a count on their pinned tab or favourite.
  • Translation keeps up as a page changes, reaches into frames, and can translate a site every time. Long pages no longer freeze while they translate.
  • VoiceOver names every control around the page and gives sidebar rows their actions.
  • Reduce Motion turns slides and zooms into fades.

Better

  • Switching tabs, crossfades and dragging split dividers are smoother.
  • Picture in Picture always uses Artemis's own mini-player.
  • A page that keeps crashing now says so, with a Reload button, instead of reloading over and over.

Fixed

  • Routing rules, addresses and cards changed just before quitting could be lost.
  • A backup that couldn't be saved or read failed without saying so.

item.title: Artemis 0.9.6
item.description:
It needs macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon.

New in 0.9.6

  • Extensions in incognito. Each extension now has an Allow in incognito switch in Settings › Extensions, off by default. Extensions that ask never to run in incognito won't, and an extension you allow there can't write your incognito pages into history.

item.title: Artemis 0.9.5
item.description:
A fix release. It needs macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon.

Fixed in 0.9.5

  • Artemis could crash on launch when there was no page to restore, for example on a fresh install. Fixed.

New

  • AppleScript and Shortcuts can list and control Artemis's windows, spaces and tabs. Running JavaScript inside pages from a script stays off unless you turn it on in Settings › Privacy.

item.title: Artemis 0.9.4
item.description:
A quick follow-up to 0.9.3. It needs macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon.

Fixed in 0.9.4

  • The download animation now actually shows: the file flies from where you clicked into the Library button.
  • With the sidebar hidden, downloads appear in a small pill at the window's bottom-left, and the file flies there instead.

item.title: Artemis 0.9.3
item.description:
The fourth alpha of Artemis for macOS. It needs macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon.

New in 0.9.3

  • Downloads you can see. A new download flies from where you clicked into the Library button, a ring around it fills as it arrives, and a pill above the sidebar footer shows the file, its progress and a tick when it's done. Click it to open the file (⌘-click shows it in Finder). The Dock icon counts running downloads.
  • Check for Updates is in the command bar (⌘T, type "update"), as well as the Artemis menu.
  • The address bar stays put properly when the sidebar opens or closes under it.

If you're on 0.9.2, this arrives on its own: look for Relaunch to Update at the bottom of the sidebar.

item.title: Artemis 0.9.2
item.description:
The third alpha of Artemis for macOS. It needs macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon.

New in 0.9.2

  • Automatic updates. From this version on, Artemis updates itself: new versions download quietly, then a Relaunch to Update button appears in the sidebar. Choose Release or Beta in Settings › General › Updates.
  • Send Feedback (Help menu) now posts your message as a public issue here, so you can follow it. Your email, screenshot and page address always stay private, and Keep this private posts nothing public.

If you're on 0.9.1, download this one by hand once; after that, updates arrive on their own.

Opening it the first time: this build isn't notarised by Apple yet, so macOS stops it the first time. Open System Settings › Privacy & Security, click Open Anyway next to Artemis, then click Open. You only do this once.
